# HTTP API

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:gen` (scripts/docs/reference.ts). Do not edit by hand. -->

Every route `notesd` serves on `127.0.0.1:7317`. The list comes from the daemon's own route table;
the descriptions live in `scripts/docs/httpRoutes.ts`, and `npm test` fails when a route has none.

## Health and MCP

The daemon listens on `127.0.0.1` only and has no authentication. Three guards recur below. **Same-origin only**: the request must reach a loopback host and carry an `Origin` equal to that host (the wall's own page); anything else, a plain `curl` included, gets 403 `forbidden_origin`. **Loopback only**: the request URL must name a loopback host and an `Origin`, when sent, must be loopback too (403 `forbidden_host` / `forbidden_origin`). **Hook routes** add the header `X-Notes-Capture: 1` and a JSON body to the loopback rule. Errors are JSON `{ "error": "<code>" }`; a body that is not JSON answers 400 `invalid_json`, and a body or query that fails validation answers 400 with the failing fields in `error`. Note, photo and file ids are accepted in any case, with or without the dash; a malformed one answers 400 `invalid_id` unless a row says otherwise.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /health` | `{"ok":true,"service":"notesd"}`. What `scripts/install.sh` waits for. |
| `POST /mcp` | The `notes` MCP server (streamable HTTP, stateless: one JSON-RPC exchange per request). Loopback only: 403 with a JSON-RPC error for another `Host` or a non-loopback `Origin`. The tools are in [mcp-tools.md](mcp-tools.md). |
| `GET /mcp` | 405 `Method not allowed` with `Allow: POST`. The server keeps no standalone event stream. |
| `DELETE /mcp` | 405 `Method not allowed` with `Allow: POST`. There are no MCP sessions to end. |

## Notes

Every note in an answer carries `id`, `body`, `tags`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `origin`, `images` and `files`. Guide: [wall.md](../wall.md).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/notes` | Live notes, most recently edited first: `{notes, next_cursor}`. Query: `tag` (repeatable, all must match, `#` optional), `has_image=true\|false`, `limit` (1 to 5000, default 2000), `cursor`. Sends an `ETag`; a matching `If-None-Match` answers 304 after one aggregate query. |
| `GET /api/notes/:id` | One live note. 404 `not_found` for a missing or deleted one. |
| `POST /api/notes` | `{body}`: a new note with origin `{source: "web"}`. An empty body is allowed (the wall creates the note, then the editor fills it). 201 with the note. |
| `PATCH /api/notes/:id` | `{body}`: replace the body. The old body is kept as a revision in the same transaction. 404 `not_found` for a missing or deleted note. |
| `DELETE /api/notes/:id` | Soft delete: the note goes to the recycle bin. Returns the note. 404 `not_found` when it is not live. |
| `POST /api/notes/:id/restore` | Bring a deleted note back. Restoring a live note returns it unchanged. 404 `not_found`. |
| `GET /api/tags` | Every tag of the live notes with its count and last use. Sends an `ETag`; 304 on a matching `If-None-Match`. |
| `GET /api/events` | Server-sent events for the wall: `event: note` `{op, id}` on every note change, `event: chat` `{op, thread_id, id}` on every chat change, `event: adversary` `{op, strategy_id, session_date}` on every reviewer change (`op`: `verdict`, `mark`, `toggle`, `run`). A comment line every 25 s keeps it open. Only this daemon's writes appear; the other machine's reach the wall by polling. |

## Recycle bin

Soft deletes wait here until restored or deleted forever. Delete forever exists only on these routes; no MCP tool can do it.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/bin` | Deleted notes and removed photos, newest deleted first: `{notes, images}`. Query: `tag` (repeatable, all must match). |
| `DELETE /api/bin/notes/:id` | Delete a note forever: its rows, its photos' originals and `cache/` folders, its files and its `files/<noteId>/` folder. 409 `not_deleted` when the note is not in the bin, 404 `not_found`. Same-origin only. |
| `DELETE /api/bin/images/:imageId` | Delete one removed photo forever: its row, original and `cache/<imageId>/`. 409 `not_deleted` when the photo is still in its note, 404 `not_found`. Same-origin only. |

## Photos

Originals are stored byte for byte; `thumb`, `preview` and `display` are derived copies made on first request. Uploads are multipart with a `file` field, capped at 200 MB (413 `too_large`); 400 `file_required` / `bad_multipart`, 415 when the bytes are not a supported image. A photo whose original is on the other machine has `available: false`. Guide: [wall.md](../wall.md).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/images` | Upload one picture as a new photo note; the optional `body` field is the note text. 201 `{note, created: true}`, or 200 `{note, created: false}` with the note that already holds the same bytes. |
| `POST /api/notes/:id/images` | Attach one more picture to a live note. 201 `{note, attached: true}`, or 200 `{note, attached: false}` with the note that already holds the bytes. 404 `not_found` for a missing or deleted note. |
| `DELETE /api/images/:imageId` | Remove one photo from its note (soft, it goes to the recycle bin and keeps its position). Returns the note. 404 `not_found`. |
| `POST /api/images/:imageId/restore` | Put a removed photo back at its old position. Returns the note. 409 `duplicate_image` with the holder's `note_id` when the same bytes are in another note now; 404 `not_found`. |
| `GET /api/images/:imageId` | One photo's metadata and URLs, whatever its state (live, removed, in a deleted note). 404 `not_found`. |
| `GET /api/images/:imageId/original` | The original bytes, with the original file name in `Content-Disposition: inline`. Works for photos in the bin too. 200 with `ETag` (304 on a matching `If-None-Match`), `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` when the file lives on the other machine. |
| `GET /api/images/:imageId/display` | What a browser can show: the original, or a full-resolution JPEG for HEIC, HEIF and TIFF. 200 with `ETag` (304 on a matching `If-None-Match`), `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` when the file lives on the other machine. |
| `GET /api/images/:imageId/thumb` | The 480 px wide WebP used by the wall and the gallery. 200 with `ETag` (304 on a matching `If-None-Match`), `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` when the file lives on the other machine. |
| `GET /api/images/:imageId/preview` | The JPEG with a 1568 px long edge that Claude is shown. 200 with `ETag` (304 on a matching `If-None-Match`), `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` when the file lives on the other machine. |
| `GET /api/notes/:id/original` | The original of a live note's first photo, kept for older links. Answers like the photo route; 404 `no_image` for a note without photos. |
| `GET /api/notes/:id/display` | The display copy of a live note's first photo. 404 `no_image` for a note without photos. |
| `GET /api/notes/:id/thumb` | The thumbnail of a live note's first photo. 404 `no_image` for a note without photos. |
| `GET /api/notes/:id/preview` | The preview of a live note's first photo. 404 `no_image` for a note without photos. |

## Files

Any other file attached to a note, stored byte for byte under `files/<noteId>/` with a Windows-safe name. Guide: [wall.md](../wall.md).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/notes/:id/files` | Multipart `file`, attached to a live note. 201 `{note, attached: true, kind}`, or 200 with the note that already holds the bytes. `kind` is `image` when the bytes are a picture (stored as a photo), else `file`. 413 `too_large` over 200 MB, 400 `file_required` / `bad_multipart`, 404 `not_found`. |
| `DELETE /api/files/:fileId` | Remove one file from its note (soft). Returns the note. 404 `not_found`. |
| `POST /api/files/:fileId/restore` | Put a removed file back at its old place. 409 `duplicate_file` with the holder's `note_id` when the bytes are in another note now; 404 `not_found`. |
| `GET /api/files/:fileId` | One file's metadata (`name`, `mime`, `bytes`, `host`, `available`, `extraction_status`), whatever its state. 404 `not_found`. |
| `GET /api/files/:fileId/download` | The bytes, always as an attachment (`Content-Disposition: attachment`, `nosniff`, sandbox CSP), with `ETag` and 304. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` when the file lives on the other machine. |

## Open file location

The reveal routes start Windows Explorer from WSL (`explorer.exe` with a path from `wslpath -w`). They take an id, never a path, and are same-origin only. Each answers 202 `{ok: true}` as soon as Explorer has started, 404 `not_found`, 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host`, 409 `reveal_unavailable` when this daemon cannot start Explorer, or 500 `spawn_failed`.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/capabilities` | `{reveal, movies_playback}`: whether "open file location" can work on this machine (Linux, WSL interop, `wslpath`, an Explorer binary), and whether Play can start VLC here. The wall hides the folder and play controls when false. |
| `POST /api/images/:imageId/reveal` | Open Explorer with the photo's original selected. |
| `POST /api/files/:fileId/reveal` | Open Explorer with the file selected. |
| `POST /api/notes/:id/reveal` | Open the note's `files/<noteId>/` folder when it has files (available when at least one is on this machine), else select its first photo. 404 `not_found` for a missing or deleted note, or one with neither. |

## Chat

The chat bar and the chat history page. Reads are open; edits, deletes and restores are same-origin only. Pasted chat images are stored under `chat-images/` and are never notes. Guide: [chat.md](../chat.md).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/chat` | `{message, thread_id?, reply_to?, image_ids?, note_image_ids?, project?}`: one chat turn. `message` may be empty when images come with it; at most 4 images in all. `project` (a repo) keeps a new thread to that project for good; an unknown `thread_id` starts a new thread. Answers as server-sent events: `accepted {thread_id, user_message_id}`, then `status {text}` and `delta {text}`, then `done {thread_id, user_message_id, assistant_message_id, reply_to, brain}`, or `error {error}`. The question is saved before the answer starts; the answer only when it finishes. Before the stream: 400 `invalid_reply_to` / `unknown_image`, 409 `not_on_this_machine`, 422 `unreadable_image`, 404 `reply_not_found`. This runs a real Claude agent on the owner's login. |
| `GET /api/chat/messages` | The chat timeline over all threads: `{messages, next_before}`, each page ascending. Query: `before` (the previous `next_before`), `limit`, `include_deleted=1`, `project` (only that repo's threads). 400 `invalid_cursor`. |
| `GET /api/chat/threads/:id` | One thread and its messages. Query: `include_deleted=1`. 404 `not_found`. |
| `PATCH /api/chat/messages/:id` | `{text}`: edit one of your own messages; the old text is kept as a revision. 400 `not_editable` (an answer) / `empty_text`, 404 `not_found`. Same-origin only. |
| `DELETE /api/chat/messages/:id` | Soft delete a message: `{deleted: [ids]}`. Query: `with_answer=1` on a question deletes its answer too. 404 `not_found`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/chat/messages/:id/restore` | Bring a deleted message back. 404 `not_found`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/chat/images` | Multipart `file` (and optional `source`: `wall`, the default, or `claude_code` from the notes-paste hook): store one pasted picture. 201 `{image, created: true}`, or 200 `{image, created: false}` when the same bytes are stored already. 400 `invalid_source` / `file_required`, 413 `too_large` over 50 MB, 415 `not_an_image`. |
| `GET /api/chat/images/:id` | One pasted image's metadata, with `available`. 404 `not_found`. |
| `GET /api/chat/images/:id/original` | The pasted image as uploaded. 200 with `ETag` (304 on a matching `If-None-Match`), `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` when the file lives on the other machine. |
| `GET /api/chat/images/:id/display` | The pasted image in a form a browser can show. 200 with `ETag` (304 on a matching `If-None-Match`), `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` when the file lives on the other machine. |
| `GET /api/chat/images/:id/thumb` | The pasted image's WebP thumbnail. 200 with `ETag` (304 on a matching `If-None-Match`), `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` when the file lives on the other machine. |
| `GET /api/chat/images/:id/preview` | The pasted image's JPEG preview. 200 with `ETag` (304 on a matching `If-None-Match`), `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. 404 `not_found`; 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` when the file lives on the other machine. |

## Capture and hooks

Called by the Claude Code hooks in `claude/hooks/`, never by the wall. Hook routes: loopback only, header `X-Notes-Capture: 1` (403 `capture_header_required`), `Content-Type: application/json` (415 `json_required`), 413 `too_large` past the body cap. A browser cannot send the header cross-origin without a preflight, which notesd never answers. Guide: [claude-code.md](../claude-code.md).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/capture/claude-code` | One `/n` exchange from the notes-capture hook: `{claude_session, user_uuid, prompt, answer, prompt_timestamp, answered_at, cwd?, images?}`, `images` being up to 8 `{media_type, data_base64}` of at most 20 MB each. 201 `{thread_id, user_message_id, assistant_message_id}`; 200 with `duplicate: true` when that session and prompt were captured before (nothing is written). 400 `invalid_base64`, 413 `image_too_large`, 415 `unsupported_image`. Body cap 64 MB. |
| `POST /api/sessions/hook/start` | From the notes-session hook (SessionStart): `{session, parent?, cwd?, name?, tmux?, host?, started_at?, source?}`. Upserts the session row (the node id is assigned on first sight). On `startup` or `clear` it links `parent` with source `env`; on `startup` in tmux with no better link it claims a pending spawn as `hook`. 200 `{session_id, node_id, parent_session_id, parent_node_id, parent_link_source, claimed}`. |
| `POST /api/sessions/hook/spawn` | From the notes-spawn hook (a `claude` launched by hand in tmux): `{parent, cwd, name?, host?}` records a pending spawn the child's start can claim, and prunes those older than a day. 201 `{recorded: true}`. |
| `POST /api/sessions/hook/link-note` | From the notes-link hook (after a notes write tool): `{session, note}` links the note to that session's node. Idempotent; the note itself never changes. 200 `{note_id, node_id, changed, made}`; 404 `unknown_session` / `not_found`; 409 `deleted`. |

## Projects and sessions

The project session graph. Rows come from the shared database, so they answer for either machine's sessions; transcripts and resume work only on the machine that holds the transcript (`not_on_this_machine`). A node id (`A0-3G`) is accepted in any case, with or without the dash; a malformed one answers 400 `invalid_node_id`, an unknown one 404 `not_found`. Guide: [sessions.md](../sessions.md).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/projects` | Repos that have Claude Code sessions, with session counts, live counts, last activity and the selected repo. |
| `GET /api/projects/selected` | `{repo}`: the repo picked in the sidebar, stored in the database so both machines agree. |
| `PUT /api/projects/selected` | `{repo}` (a repo or null): store the pick. 404 `unknown_repo`. Same-origin only. |
| `GET /api/projects/:repo/sessions` | That repo's sessions for the graph: node id, parent and link source (`fork`, `env`, `hook`, `heuristic`), times, name, `live`, `host`, `available`, `unfinished`. Query: `before` (a datetime), `limit` (1 to 5000, default 2000). Sends a weak `ETag` and answers 304 to a matching `If-None-Match` (the wall polls it). 404 `unknown_repo`. |
| `GET /api/sessions/context` | Session context for the notes-prompt hook. Query: `ids` (node ids separated by commas or spaces); ids that do not exist are left out. Loopback only. |
| `GET /api/sessions/known` | Which node ids exist, with their repo: `{nodes: [{node_id, repo}]}`. Query: `ids`. The wall and the note-links mod link only these. |
| `GET /api/sessions/search` | Session search, blended like note search, with `fallback` when only words were used. Query: `q` (required), `repo`, `limit` (1 to 50, default 10). Each hit carries `via_notes` and `via_replies` like the `sessions_search` tool. |
| `GET /api/sessions/usage` | Tokens and cost per session or per month. Query: `by=node\|month` (default `month`), `repo`, `month` (`YYYY-MM`), `limit` (1 to 200, default 20). |
| `GET /api/sessions/:nodeId` | One session in full: summary, prompts, commits, plan docs, files edited, its notes (made or linked), tokens and cost, parent and children, `host`, `available`, `context`, and `fork` for a fork. |
| `GET /api/sessions/:nodeId/transcript` | Passages of the transcript. Query: `query` (words to match), `limit`. On a fork only the records after the fork point are read (`starts_at_fork_point: true`). 404 `not_on_this_machine` with `host` for the other machine's session. |
| `GET /api/sessions/:nodeId/prompts` | Every stored prompt of a session, numbered, in full. Read from the database, so it works for either machine. `complete: false` with `incomplete_reason` (`not_backfilled`, `transcript_pruned`) when only excerpts are kept. |
| `GET /api/sessions/:nodeId/context` | The session's current context: `{node_id, host, available, context}`, `context` being `{tokens, window, percent, band, model, at, window_source, peak_tokens}` or null when no main-chain reply with token usage was seen. `band` is `green` below 40 %, `amber` below 70 %, `red` from 70 %. Works for either machine. |
| `GET /api/sessions/:nodeId/context/stream` | Server-sent events: one `context` event with the same JSON on connect, another whenever this machine's ingest stores a reply that changes tokens, model or window, and heartbeats. The other machine's sessions send only the first event, so the wall polls the JSON route for those. |
| `POST /api/sessions/:nodeId/summarize` | Ask for a summary now. Records the request only; the owning machine's summary worker serves it first on its next pass. `{node_id, summary_state, summary_requested_at}`; repeating it is a no-op. 409 `empty_session` for a session with no tokens. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/sessions/:nodeId/resume` | `{prompt?, fresh?}` (unknown keys are refused, 400 `invalid_body`): open the session again in a new tmux window, or switch to it when it is live. 200 `{action, window?, cwd?, original_cwd?, job_id?, prompt_delivered?}` with `action` one of `focused`, `messaged`, `resumed`, `spawned`, `attached`. `fresh: true` writes a handoff file under `handoffs/` and starts a new session with it; a live background job gets a `claude attach <job>` window. 404 `not_on_this_machine`, 409 `no_tmux` / `live_outside_tmux`, 500 `spawn_failed`. Same-origin only. |
| `GET /api/sessions/:nodeId/handoff` | Dry run of "Spawn fresh": `{node_id, tokens, window, percent, baseline, exchanges_included, exchanges_total, truncated}`, the estimated starting context of the new session. Writes no file and runs no git; works for either machine. |

## Seer Adversarial

The read model over Seer's database plus the reviewer's switch. Reads work with `NOTESD_ADVERSARY=off`; they answer 503 `seer_unavailable` (`detail`: `not_reachable`, `not_migrated`, `query_failed`) when Seer cannot be read. A method id is accepted in any case and a twin's id means its original; 400 `invalid_id`, 404 `not_found`. Guide: [adversary.md](../adversary.md).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/adversary/overview` | Every method with its Claude twin and SPY: `roster`, `methods` (returns, objections, coverage, checklists), `cause`, `latest`, `last_review`, `reviewer`. |
| `GET /api/adversary/methods/:id` | One method: curves, stats, checklists, the current decision's verdict cards, every decision, the objection record, revisions, and the three-way comparison for a daily method. |
| `GET /api/adversary/methods/:id/decisions/:session` | One decision's verdict cards (`session` is a date): reason, sources, host, `late`, weight and twin weight. 400 `invalid_session`. |
| `GET /api/adversary/daily/:id` | The three-way for a daily method on one session: the ranked list with both verdicts, what each book bought, the disagreement grid. Query: `session` (default: the latest). 400 `not_bracket` for a method that is not daily. |
| `GET /api/adversary/scorecard/:id` | Each objection's return over the method's horizon against the kept picks, and, for a daily method, Claude against C on the nights they disagree. |
| `GET /api/adversary/toggle` | Whether automatic reviews are on, a switch kept in the shared database that both machines obey. 503 `reviewer_off` when this daemon has no reviewer. |
| `PUT /api/adversary/toggle` | `{on}`: turn automatic reviews on or off. 503 `reviewer_off`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/adversary/review-now` | `{strategy_id?}`: start one review pass now, even while automatic reviews are off. 202 `{started, reason}` before it finishes (`reason` says when it queued behind a running pass). 503 `reviewer_off`. Same-origin only. |

## Movies

With `NOTESD_MOVIES=off` every route here answers 503 `movies_off`, except `GET /api/movies/player`, which answers `{available: false, reason: "movies_off"}`. Titles are shared by both machines; files, plays and VLC belong to one. Writes and anything that starts VLC are same-origin only. Guide: [movies.md](../movies.md).

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/movies` | The library: `{titles}`, one entry per title with `poster_url` and its derived `state`. Query: `q` (full text over title and synopsis), `state`, `kind=movie\|tv`, `company`, `person`, `finished_from`, `finished_to`, `sort` (default `recent`), `limit`. |
| `GET /api/movies/unmatched` | This machine's files that are not in the library: `{files}`, each with its `reason` (`too_short`, `no_match`, `low_confidence`, `tmdb_error`, `no_tmdb_credentials`, `probe_failed`). |
| `GET /api/movies/status` | Whether the library is on, its roots, the last pass with its counts, and `counts` of titles and files. |
| `GET /api/movies/search-tmdb` | TMDB search, for picking the title of an unmatched file: `{results}`. Query: `q` (required), `kind=movie\|tv`, `year`. 503 `tmdb_off` without credentials, 502 `tmdb_error`. |
| `GET /api/movies/events` | Server-sent events: `event: changed` after every pass or write that changes the library, and heartbeats. |
| `GET /api/movies/:movieId` | One title by movie id (`M-23T4`, any case). An episode's movie id answers its series. Same body as the route below. 404 `not_found`. |
| `GET /api/movies/:id` | One title by key (`movie-<tmdb id>` or `tv-<tmdb id>`): release date, synopsis, studios, crew, cast, rating, watched, review, the episode list, and every file (deleted ones too) with its `state`, `available`, season and episode. 404 `not_found`. |
| `POST /api/movies/:id/user` | `{watched?, rating?, review?}` (at least one): the watched flag, 0 to 5 stars or null, and the review, which is kept as a note tagged `#movie` and linked to the title. Returns the title. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/movies/files/:fileId/watched` | `{watched}`: mark one file or episode finished, or take the mark off. `{file_id, title}`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/movies/files/:fileId/assign` | `{kind, tmdb_id, season?, episode?}` (season and episode together, `tv` only): put an unmatched or wrongly matched file under that TMDB title. 503 `tmdb_off`, 502 `tmdb_error`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/movies/sync` | Start a library pass now: 202 `{started: true, report: null}`. Query: `wait=true` answers 200 with the pass report when it ends. Same-origin only. |
| `GET /api/movies/player` | `{available, reason, current}`: whether playback works on this machine and the play notesd is following now, if any. |
| `POST /api/movies/files/:fileId/play` | Start VLC on the file at its resume point (the last position; the start when there is none or it was finished). 202 `{ok: true, play}`. 404 `not_found` / `not_on_this_machine`, 410 `file_missing`, 409 `player_unavailable` with `reason`. Same-origin only. |
| `POST /api/movies/continue` | `{title?}`: what the `movies_continue` tool does: resume the latest unfinished episode or film, else start the next episode that is here. Without `title`, the title of the newest play. Same errors as play; 400 `invalid_body`. Same-origin only. |
| `GET /api/movies/player/health` | This machine's VLC health log: the newest samples, per-VLC run summaries, hang lines and crash incidents. Query: `limit` (samples, 1 to 2000, default 200; 400 `invalid_limit`). 503 `movies_off` without a monitor. |

## Debug

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/debug/egress` | Rows and approximate bytes returned per query shape since the daemon started, largest first, plus the Neon quota breaker (`quota.tripped`, `quota.resumes_at`). `{enabled: false}` with `NOTESD_EGRESS_METER=off`. Loopback only. See [architecture.md](../architecture.md#neon). |
